===== SPEC =====
# shortener

An HTTP API that turns long URLs into short codes and redirects visitors who open a code.

## Running

Start the server with `node dist/server.js`. It listens on the port in the `PORT` environment variable (default `3000`). State is kept in memory. Every response with a body is JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`. Errors have the body `{"error": "<message>"}`.

## Link

```
{"code": "docs", "url": "https://example.com/docs", "hits": 0, "createdAt": "2026-10-30T09:12:44.512Z"}
```

`createdAt` is the creation time in ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds, as produced by `Date.prototype.toISOString`. `hits` counts the redirects served for the code.

## Endpoints

### `POST /links`

Body: `{"url": "<string>", "code": "<string, optional>"}`. Checked in this order; the first failure is the response:

1. The body must be a JSON object, otherwise `400 {"error": "body must be a JSON object"}`.
2. `url` must be a string holding an absolute URL whose scheme is `http` or `https`, otherwise `400 {"error": "url must be an absolute http(s) URL"}`.
3. `code`, when present, must be a string of 4 to 32 characters from `A`-`Z`, `a`-`z`, `0`-`9`, `_` and `-`, and must not be `links`; otherwise `400 {"error": "invalid code"}`.

Then:

- A `code` nobody uses: the link is created, `201` with the link.
- A `code` that already exists with the same `url`: nothing changes, `200` with the existing link.
- A `code` that already exists … [1379 more]

items.statement: Server started with `node dist/server.js` listens on PORT env var, default 3000. State in memory.
Every response with a body is JSON with Content-Type application/json; errors have body {"error": "<message>"}.
Link object has fields code (string), url (string), hits (integer count of redirects), createdAt (ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds from toISOString).
POST /links: body must be a JSON object (not array, null, string, number, or invalid JSON), else 400 {"error":"body must be a JSON object"}. Checked first.
POST /links: url must be a string that is an absolute URL with scheme http or https, else 400 {"error":"url must be an absolute http(s) URL"}. Checked second (after body check, before code check).
POST /links: code, when present, must be a string of 4-32 chars from A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -, and not equal to 'links'; else 400 {"error":"invalid code"}. Checked third.
POST /links with unused code creates link (hits 0) and returns 201 with the link.
POST /links with existing code and same url: no change, 200 with existing link.
POST /links with existing code and different url: 409 {"error":"code already in use"}.
POST /links without code: if a link with exactly this url exists, 200 with the oldest such link; otherwise create with random 6-char alphanumeric code and return 201.
URLs compared as exact strings with no normalisation; https://a.example and https://a.example/ are different (stored url is returned as given).
GET /links/:code returns 200 with the link or 404 {"error":"not found"}; does not increment hits.
GET /:code returns 302 with Location header equal to link url and increments hits by one; unknown code gives 404 {"error":"not found"}.
DELETE /links/:code returns 204 with empty body and frees the code for reuse; unknown code gives 404 {"error":"not found"}.
Any other method or path gives 404 {"error":"not found"} (e.g. GET /links, PUT /links/x, POST /x, nested paths).
